requirements.text: Turn the image into a drawing made from chalk
requirements.source_phrase: Turn the image into a drawing made from chalk

outcomes.description: Transform the image into a chalk drawing.

nodes.question: Does the edited image convincingly render the depicted scene in a chalk medium, rather than merely adding chalk-like grain or smudging to photographic content?
nodes.criteria: pass: chalk marks and surface treatment convincingly render the depicted forms and scene as chalk, not just as a texture overlay; fail: visible chalk-like texture is only an overlay on substantially photographic content, or no chalk treatment is evident; unknown: the image does not provide enough visual evidence to distinguish these cases.
nodes.binding: Assess only whether the depicted scene is rendered in a chalk medium; texture alone is insufficient. Do not assess drawing conversion independently of the chalk treatment.

nodes.question: Do the depicted forms visibly read as drawn, rather than as photographic forms with softened contours or sketch-like shading?
nodes.criteria: pass: the forms themselves are convincingly rendered as drawn, with drawing cues across the depicted content; fail: substantial photographic detail remains and the apparent drawing effect is limited to softened contours, shading, or an overlay; unknown: the image does not establish whether the forms read as drawn or photographic.
nodes.binding: Assess only drawing conversion of the depicted forms, using the source and edited images; do not assess chalk medium.

nodes.question: Has the image been transformed into a drawing made from chalk?
nodes.criteria: complete: both supports pass, establishing convincing chalk-medium rendering and drawing conversion. partial: at least one support passes and the other fails or is unknown, evidencing some requested progress but not complete fulfillment. absent: both supports fail, and their evidence establishes that neither chalk-medium rendering nor drawing conversion has progressed. unknown: no support passes and at least one is unknown, or the support evidence does not establish whether any requested progress occurred. A support failure is not by itself proof of absence; do not infer facts beyond saved evidence.
nodes.binding: Target: the image. Reference: a drawing made from chalk. Combine the independent evidence for chalk medium and drawing form; do not inspect images or add requirements.

program.checker_template:
Execute ONE saved check. Return status, evidence, confidence (0 to 1 or null), and used_dependency_ids. You receive no reference label or optimizer feedback. Do not predict what the optimizer wants.
Support checks receive source and edited images. Inspect only the saved visual proposition and binding. When dependencies are supplied, use those ancestor observations as context and investigate the more specific proposition yourself; do not simply repeat the parent answer. Use pass/fail/unknown. A pass on a broad parent does not imply a nested check passes. Known negative evidence is usable; uncertain or missing evidence is unknown. Do not award requested completion credit to supporting facts.
The requested fulfillment readout receives NO images. Use ALL and ONLY saved support observations, the original instruction, rubric and saved composition criteria. Use complete/partial/absent/unknown. Mere texture or object presence must not silently establish whole-image conversion or a requested spatial relation. Known progress plus evidenced incompleteness may be partial; absence means no requested progress. Missing necessary evidence is unknown, never a fabricated failure or completion. Do not infer new visual facts.
used_dependency_ids must name every supplied dependency check_id exactly once in saved order (empty when none). Confidence is self-report, not calibrated correctness.
